Subject: FinLedger discovery — SLO readiness & graceful-degradation recap

Thanks again for the time today, Alex. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we have alignment. I tried to keep the items action-oriented.

Pain points you mentioned
- Repeated latency spikes during scheduled batch runs that cascade into job timeouts for downstream analytics.
- Failover to backup region has gaps: two of the last three incidents required manual intervention and took ~7 minutes to restore.
- Limited token-level observability — engineering can’t easily attribute cost to specific features or routes.

What success looks like (criteria you shared)
- P99 generation latency <= 300ms for typical 512-token workloads under normal traffic.
- Cross-region failover completes automatically within 30s for critical routes, with graceful fallback to a smaller compatible model if full capacity isn’t available.
- Transparent per-route cost reporting and token-level breakdown for monthly budget reconciliation.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll share a Mutual Action Plan (attached) that outlines a 6-week pilot: metrics, test traffic, and SLA targets.
2) You’ll share the last-quarter incident logs and current SLO targets so we can validate assumptions (you mentioned ops@finledger is collecting these).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra lead + Redwood runtime engineer to validate failover and KV-cache behavior.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, incident_summaries.pdf (summary of what we discussed)

Proposed meeting windows: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT or 2–4 PT — I’ll leave it to you which works.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on a pilot that focuses on graceful degradation and measurable SLO uplift.

Monica — thanks for the tidy summary. Confirming a few specifics from our side that will help the MAP be practical:

Incident history (last 3 months)
- 2027-01-12: us-west1 degraded routing -> backup region failover executed but required manual DNS bump; user-facing downtime ~7m.
- 2027-02-24: autoscaling misconfiguration during a marketing spike caused queueing and 503s for 9m.

Current internal SLO posture
- p50: 90ms, p90: 180ms, p99: 620ms (this is where you saw spikes).
- We currently target a 99.5% availability SLA for customer-facing APIs but have internal tolerance for longer tails during heavy batch windows.

Additional notes
- We run a mixed fleet: priority production traffic in us-west1 + a smaller standby fleet in us-east1. Failover is generally automated but the DNS TTL/health-check coupling is brittle.
- We can provide the raw incident logs: finledger_incidents_q1.log (attaching) and our SLO definitions (.csv) if helpful.

We’re happy to share the ops lead — cc’d ops@finledger.com — and can target Wed 4/7 for the deep-dive if that works on your end.

Regards,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLedger

Short update — drafted the pilot outline below and can expand into the one-pager by EOD Tue. We should be able to present this on Wed’s deep-dive.

Pilot sketch (6 weeks)
- Deployment: Dedicated small pool in us-west1 for baseline traffic, standby pool in us-east1; canary routing 10% -> 50% over two weeks.
- Fallbacks: configure per-route policy to failover first to a quantized small model (redwood-small-v1) in-region, then cross-region to standby pool if KV-cache warmup fails.
- SLAs/SLOs: target p99 <= 300ms for designated critical routes; fallback latency target for redwood-small-v1 <= 450ms with semantic match >=95% measured via eval prompts.
- Observability: enable token-level cost logging for pilot routes + early dashboard access for FinLedger.

Preliminary pricing notes (Rishi to validate)
- Estimate: reserved baseline + capped hourly burst; pilot expected to run ~$28k–$40k depending on sustained traffic during the test window. We can tighten after profile data.

Next steps
- Rishi to confirm pricing and any SLA carve-outs.
- Monica to finalize Wed 4/7 deep-dive invite with FinLedger ops lead.

Happy to sync offline if you want to adjust routing numbers.

—Karithik
